findings.label: Thirteen timing workloads sit on a ~64-67 us per-call submission floor that the single device task cannot explain

evidence.metric: Block Num (programs) and steady-state kernel duration for [1,2048]
evidence.value: 1 program; 1.44-1.62 us per launch; consecutive Task Start Time entries 78-90 us apart with Task Wait Time ~80 us

evidence.metric: device task types present in the timeline
evidence.value: AI_VECTOR_CORE only (stream tid=5), plus 2 setup events PROFILING_ENABLE/TASK_TIMEOUT_SET on tid=20; no memcpy/DMA rows and no host rows

evidence.metric: avg_duration_us for [512,2048] (64 blocks) vs eval latency 0.06362 ms
avg_duration_us for [4096,2048] (512 blocks) vs eval latency 0.06672 ms

findings.inference: Each call issues exactly one device task (operation_count=1 for every profiled workload), so the fused kernel is intact and no cast/copy/extra kernel was added. But for [1,2048] the device task is 1.905 us against 65.61 us of eval latency, for [512,2048] 7.573 us against 63.62 us, and for [4096,2048] 37.60 us against 66.72 us. A single model fits all five profiled workloads: latency ~= max(~65 us per-call host submission, device duration) - 125.8 us device -> 127.0 us eval and 262.5 us device -> 261.8 us eval show the host cost is fully hidden once device work exceeds it. So 12 of 15 timing workloads (00000-00012) are still host-submission bound by roughly 60-65 us per call, and the round-3 cached launcher lowered the floor from ~127 us to ~65 us without removing it. The msprof trace records only device tasks, so this artifact set cannot decompose the residual 65 us into torch.empty, key/dict lookup, stream query, launch_metadata or the run ABI call. Eval latency values are taken from the trusted round-3 snapshot, not from profiler timing.

findings.label: The two largest workloads are device-bound with the Vector pipe as the largest active pipe

evidence.metric: avg_duration_us and Block Num for [4096,16384] (4096x16384 bf16 in / 4096x8192 bf16 out)
evidence.value: 262.513 us over 2048 programs; eval latency 0.26178 ms

evidence.metric: per-launch spacing versus kernel duration in the same trace
evidence.value: Task Start Time deltas ~262-263 us with Task Wait Time 0.0-0.2 us, i.e. no host gap

findings.inference: For 00013/00014 the eval latency equals the device duration to within ~1 us, and the Vector pipe is the largest active pipe at 0.80/0.76 while MTE2 is only 0.12/0.17 and MTE3 0.06. This makes the element-wise activation arithmetic in the fp32 GELU expression (lines 75-78) the leading candidate for these two workloads, not load bandwidth. The marginal ratios sum to ~1.03, so they must not be read as a timeline split or as proven Vector saturation; no instruction-level artifact exists this round to confirm which vector operations dominate. Program counts (2048 programs for 00014 over 20 AI cores, ~102 waves) do not indicate a tail-imbalance problem severe enough to explain the gap.

findings.label: Streaming access is already tile-contiguous; no redundant cast or copy kernels are issued

evidence.metric: device task count per call (single op row per invocation)
MTE2/MTE3 active share at 37.6 us device time [4096,2048]

findings.inference: The reference path in the frozen paired evidence consumed 5 device kernels (2 casts, GELU, Mul, cast), whereas the candidate issues one. With MTE2 at 0.10-0.17 and MTE3 at 0.06-0.07 on the largest shapes, there is no counter evidence of a load/store bottleneck or of fine-grained transfer; the per-program tile is a contiguous ROWS x BLOCK_C block, so the docstring claim of contiguous MTE transactions is consistent with the reports. This rules out 'add more bandwidth/prefetch' as the next lever for these shapes.

performance_interpretation: Round 3 raised geo_mean from 1.3118 to 2.2671 (+72.8%) by moving the per-call floor from ~0.123-0.129 ms to ~0.063-0.067 ms, which the profiler now shows is still ~64-67 us of host submission wrapped around a 1.9-37.6 us device task. Thirteen of the fifteen timing workloads remain dispatch-bound; only 00013 (0.127 ms) and 00014 (0.262 ms) are limited by device execution, and there the Vector pipe is the largest active pipe. Because geo_mean averages per-workload speedups and 13 workloads sit in the dispatch band, further reduction of the host floor carries far more geo_mean leverage than improving the two large shapes. The frozen round-3 hypothesis (caching the compiled kernel would remove ~28 us per call) is supported and exceeded on the flat band (0.1276 -> 0.0656 ms), but its predicted end state of 0.09-0.10 ms did not materialise and the profiler shows a residual floor the hypothesis did not account for. No numeric Roofline is asserted: there is no matched physical byte count, hardware ceiling or instruction artifact for these workloads.

next_experiment.action_description: Reduce the remaining per-call host submission cost of the cached-launch fast path in .kernelgen/evals/round-0003/main.py, in two steps that stay inside the existing fallback contract. (1) Bounded host probe first (Debug Job, no formal eval): instrument the fast path with perf_counter around torch.empty, the key build + dict lookup, _driver.active.get_current_stream, kernel.launch_metadata, and kernel.run, plus end-to-end wrapper walltime, on [1,2048] and [4096,2048]; require >=1000 iterations and report medians so the residual ~65 us is attributed to a measured sub-step rather than guessed. (2) Apply the single change those numbers justify; the candidate already implied by upstream Triton semantics is to stop building launch metadata when no profiler hook is attached - compute metadata = kernel.launch_metadata(grid, stream, *args) only when _knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook is not None and pass None otherwise - and to prebuild the constant (half, block_c, rows, even_cols) argument tuple once in _PreboundLaunch.__init__, inlining the launch into the wrapper to drop one Python frame and repeated attribute loads. Keep reading the current stream and the enter/exit hooks on every call, keep passing live x/out tensors (never cache pointers or tensors), and keep the normal kernel[grid](...) fallback on any mismatch or exception.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the residual floor is Python-level work inside the wrapper, cutting it from ~65 us toward the ~35 us measured in the round-3 probe would move the 13 dispatch-bound workloads from 0.063-0.067 ms to roughly 0.040-0.050 ms, i.e. their speedups from ~1.92-2.15x to ~2.6-3.0x and geo_mean from 2.267 to about 2.6-2.9. If the probe shows the residual is dominated by the launcher ABI call or by work outside the wrapper, the expected gain is near zero and the hypothesis is falsified for this round.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Dropping launch metadata must not break profiling: the batch requires the profiler-compatible metadata path, so the None branch may only be taken when both hooks are absent, and the standard metadata path must remain reachable and exercised by the next metrics collection. Prebuilding the argument tuple must exclude x, out and any per-call pointer; a tuple that captures tensors would alias a previous call's buffers and break correctness on differently shaped or offset inputs. The change is host-only and must not alter kernel math, tile shape or grid, so rollback is dropping the cached-path edits and keeping the round-3 logic. A launcher registration failure must still not re-execute the kernel a second time.
success_criteria: The host probe attributes the residual floor to a named sub-step with medians over >=1000 iterations on [1,2048] and [4096,2048].

The four frozen correctness workloads still pass with the original tolerance, and the independent 18-item layout/value semantics plus the 15 timing-input value checks still pass, two runs each with a stream switch.
The profiled call still issues exactly one AI_VECTOR_CORE device task per invocation with the same kernel name and unchanged per-program tile.
metrics collection still completes on the modified source (non-empty op_summary and a completed profiling marker), proving the metadata branch is still correct under the profiler.

Median latency of the 13 dispatch-bound workloads falls below ~0.055 ms without regressing 00013/00014, and full KGS geo_mean exceeds 2.2671 with the reference comparison recomputed in the same round.

warnings: msprof durations and simulator timing are diagnostic and are not eval latency; all speedup and latency figures in this analysis come from the frozen evaluation snapshot of round 3.
The AI Vector pipe active ratios are marginal activity shares; they do not sum to a timeline decomposition and are not peak utilization.

The execution trace contains no host/Python events, so the launch-bound conclusion rests on the device task count and the device-duration/eval-latency ratio, not on a resolved timeline of host sub-steps.
No quantitative Roofline is asserted for any workload: matched physical byte counts, hardware ceilings and instruction artifacts are absent.
open_questions: How much of the ~65 us per-call floor is inside the wrapper versus the evaluation harness's own per-call work? The msprof trace for this round contains only device tasks (AI_VECTOR_CORE) and profiler setup events, with no host-side rows, so this cannot be answered from the collected artifacts.

Which vector operations dominate the 0.76-0.80 Vector active share on 00013/00014 (fp32 cubic, sigmoid/exp, reciprocal, or the bf16<->fp32 conversions)? No instruction-level artifact was collected this round; a bounded instruction request on a small shape would be needed to separate them.

Does the fixed ~65 us floor come mostly from the private launch ABI call itself? The round-3 probe measured 35.3 us for the same cached launch on [1,2048] while this round's eval latency is 65.6 us, so part of the floor plausibly sits outside the candidate's control.
